items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: Rogers & Hammerstein, all of that they license.

ctx.x: It means a lot of money.

It means a hell of a lot of money. At that point it was $350,000 was the budget. And that’s nowhere near what it would be today. And so the publishers, now Samuel French did publish a childrens’ show, The Great Gray Ghost of Old Spook Lane. Anyway I went to talk to them recently and I couldn’t find them, because they have now been bought by Concord Theatricals. Concord Theatricals is another big — it was Concord Records the jazz label originally, of California. But it has grown and it now owns Andrew Lloyd Weber,…
